counterfactual_missing_items: No left atrial appendage thrombus or alternative cardiac embolic source was documented
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery could independently contribute to ischemia
Mechanical thrombectomy achieved reperfusion but no clinical improvement
decisive_items: acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2
Twenty-four-hour Holter monitoring confirmed atrial fibrillation
response.rationale: R7 yields a specific cardioembolic mechanism by linking confirmed persistent atrial fibrillation without anticoagulation to the acute left MCA occlusion. R3 is the appropriate fallback because it names the ischemic stroke but omits the causal source; R6 and R8 are coexisting findings without direct causal linkage to the acute stroke, and R2 is weakened by normal ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

rejected.why: Hypertension and LVH are risk factors, but ABPM was normal and no hypertensive mechanism explains the acute MCA occlusion.
Severe low-gradient aortic stenosis is present, but there is no direct link to the acute left MCA occlusion; AF is the more proximate embolic source.
Pulmonary emboli are present, but no paradoxical embolism or PFO is documented, and they do not explain the acute left MCA stroke.
